crime_highlights: Mr. Peters started to punch him and repeatedly stomped on Mr. Leo's head, smashing it into the ground
He then grabbed Mr. Leo's head and rammed it into the ground numerous times
He kicked Mr. Leo in the head until he could no longer get up
The pathology report said that there had been up to 15 blows. Death was caused by trauma to the head.
rationale_highlights: the judge noted the message from the Supreme Court of Canada in Gladue
he was taking into account the principles of deterrence, the principles of aboriginal sentencing, and all of the subjective elements argued before him
note: Appeal court only notes aboriginal sentencing principles were considered; no reasoning on effect.

crime_highlights: an undercover officer purchased several flaps of cocaine for two hundred and forty dollars
On his person they found a baggie containing 24.7 grams of cocaine and a wallet with six hundred and sixty dollars in cash in it
they found scales, twenty-two empty prepared flaps, and cocaine residue
rationale_highlights: there are special considerations when dealing with aboriginal offenders
poor social circumstances, including poverty, lack of education and job skills and lack of opportunity, all of which are related to his aboriginal ancestry and status
I would not accede to the appellant's claims that the trial judge failed to take into account the appellant's aboriginal ancestry
note: Court rejects ground; no evidence of circumstances; no reduction of culpability stated. Crime narrative is inside quoted trial reasons.

crime_highlights: he had in his possession four baggies of cocaine with a total weight of 116 grams and which had a street value of approximately $10,000
He also had in his possession a detailed score sheet showing previous one ounce sales and over $900 in cash
rationale_highlights: it nevertheless remains necessary to consider the individual circumstances of the offender and the offence
he is aboriginal and was exposed to family violence, alcohol abuse, poverty and discrimination
the sentencing judge failed to give adequate consideration to the facts

Had the sentencing judge given adequate consideration to those mitigating factors, I think he would have concluded that a conditional sentence would have been consistent with the fundamental purpose and principles of sentencing
note: Crime passage short (under 120 words); thin facts.
